text:
maria_cs: FYI - ACME reported a weird combo: embeddings work but generation and rerank calls get 403. Customer says they were provisioned via SSO service-key flow last week. Pasting their repro below. Can someone triage?

acme_support_snippet (pasted by maria_cs):
```
# embeddings OK
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-prod-xxxx" \
  -d '{"model":"embed-lite","input":"hello"}'
# returns 200 and vectors

# generation fails
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-prod-xxxx" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-redwood","prompt":"hi"}'
# returns 403
{"error":{"code":403,"message":"missing required scope(s): generation, rerank"}}
```

maria_cs: Customer is blocked - workspace is production, they're on Dedicated trial. They need generation for chat features and rerank for search. They say admin UI shows the key has scopes: embeddings, rerank, but game-time calls disagree.

alex_eng: thanks - can you paste the exact service key id (not the secret)? we need to correlate with provisioning logs. Also what auth flow created it (Okta SCIM connector vs manual service key)?

maria_cs: Key id: svc_01F7XYZ. Provisioned via SSO connector (Okta SCIM) by their SRE on 2025-11-02. I redacted secret but included id and sample curl above.

jonas_platform: taking a look at provisioning audit. Quick check: svc_01F7XYZ maps to org_id: org-acme, created by connector: okta-scim, role: "app_readwrite". In our provisioner, roles map to scopes via mapping table role_scope_map. I see an entry for "app_readwrite" -> ["embeddings","rerank"] but not "generation". That would explain generation missing but rerank should be allowed - odd that rerank is called out too.

priya_se: got it. Possible race: when we rolled out the granular scopes toggle last month, older service keys sometimes have an internal flag scope_version=1 and provisioning API will surface legacy scopes incorrectly to the UI. UI shows cached desired scopes but runtime checks token metadata for allowed_scopes array. Can you paste the raw token introspection output from the runtime? Maria, can you ask the customer to hit the introspect endpoint:

```
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-prod-xxxx" \
  https://auth.redwood.ai/v1/introspect | jq .
# expect: {"active":true, "scopes":["embeddings","rerank"]}
```

maria_cs: I asked customer to run and they returned:
```
{"active":true, "scopes":["embeddings"]}
```

maria_cs: so UI showed rerank too but introspection shows only embeddings. So runtime rejects both generation and rerank. Customer surprised because admin console showed rerank present.

alex_eng: ok this points to provisioning-sync bug. Possible causes:
1) SCIM connector sent group -> role mapping that included rerank, but our sync job failed midway and only wrote embeddings scope to token cache.
2) There's a stale cache in auth runtime (redis key svc:scopes:svc_01F7XYZ) that hasn't picked up latest mapping.

jonas_platform: checking sync logs now. I see a 2025-11-02 sync job for org-acme that logged an error "partial-write on scopes array" at 03:14 UTC, followed by retries and eventual success 03:19. But the success event wrote to the provisioning DB (postgres) - however there was a later background job (scope-updater) that failed to publish change to redis (error: timeout contacting redis-cluster-2). That would leave runtime reading an older cached value.

priya_se: mitigation steps for customer:
- temporary: create a new service key via the admin UI (manual service key) with required scopes (generation, rerank, embeddings). New key should bypass SCIM sync and be immediately introspectable. Command in prod console: `POST /admin/orgs/org-acme/service_keys` body: {"scopes":["generation","rerank","embeddings"]}
- medium: force a resync of their SCIM connector in our provisioner (we have an endpoint /provisioner/resync?org=org-acme) - requires platform approval.

maria_cs: Customer prefers not to create new keys (policy). They asked for a platform-side resync + confirm fix. They also asked for ETA and whether their current key will be invalidated.

jonas_platform: I can trigger a manual resync and monitor redis publish. Plan:
1) run resync for org-acme (no downtime) - timestamp 1958765600
2) validate introspect output & runtime cache
3) if publish fails due to redis, we'll failover to secondary redis and republish
I'll post logs and IDs. ETA 30-45m.

alex_eng: longer term, we should add a reconciliation check: background job compares postgres scopes vs redis cache every 6h and alerts on mismatch. Also add a one-button "refresh runtime cache" in admin UI.

provisioner-bot: ACTION LOG: resync requested by jonas_platform for org-acme at 1958765700; creating task rsync-5632.

jonas_platform: resync started. logs:
```
[1958765731] rsync-5632: fetch scim groups -> ok
[1958765740] rsync-5632: map roles -> ok
[1958765742] rsync-5632: write postgres scopes -> ok
[1958765750] rsync-5632: publish redis key svc:scopes:svc_01F7XYZ -> ERROR: timeout
[1958765760] rsync-5632: retry publish -> SUCCESS (sent to redis-cluster-3)
```

maria_cs: customer re-ran introspect, they sent back:
```
{"active":true, "scopes":["embeddings","rerank","generation"]}
```

maria_cs: they also tried the generate endpoint and it's working now. Customer very happy. They asked for a postmortem and permanent fix.

priya_se: please capture details for a postmortem: race condition between scope-updater and redis cluster availability; root cause: redis-cluster-2 had elevated latency during their resync windows causing publish timeouts. Remediation:
- short-term: add retry with exponential backoff (we have already retried once automatically)
- medium: add reconciliation job (alex suggestion)
- long-term: make runtime consult postgres if redis claim misses (read-through fallback).

alex_eng: i'll own the reconciliation job RFC and add a dashboard alert for mismatched scope counts. ETA RFC by EOD.

jonas_platform: closing loop with customer. I'll also add a note to internal runbook for SSO-provisioned service keys and how to force-refresh cache.

maria_cs: thanks team. I'll reply to customer with steps we ran and link to upcoming PM/RFC. Marking as resolved for now. :white_check_mark:
